concerns.text: The plan computes a covariate‑adjusted Spearman correlation by first residualizing taxon‑slope and outcome‑slope on age, sex, and levodopa dose (linear regression) and then applying a Spearman rank correlation to the residuals. This is not a standard method for partial Spearman correlation; residualization changes the data scale and can distort rank relationships, potentially biasing the correlation estimate. A more appropriate approach would be to use a true partial Spearman correlation (e.g., via permutation of ranks while conditioning on covariates) or to apply a rank‑based partial correlation method. The current approach may yield misleading significance values, compromising scientific validity.
